passages.text: Some time later, David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?” “Go up,” the LORD answered. Then David asked, “Where should I go?” “To Hebron,” replied the LORD.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
David wanted to know what to do next.
David spoke to the LORD.
David asked the LORD a question.
David said, “Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?”
The LORD answered David.
The LORD said, “Go up.”
David asked another question.
David said, “Where should I go?”
The LORD replied to David.
The LORD said, “Go to Hebron.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵ֗ן וַיִּשְׁאַל֩ דָּוִ֨ד בַּֽיהוָ֤ה׀ לֵאמֹר֙ הַאֶעֱלֶ֗ה בְּאַחַת֙ עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו עֲלֵ֑ה וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אָ֥נָה אֶעֱלֶ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חֶבְרֹֽנָה׃

passages.text: So David went there with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader chosen by God.
David went to Hebron.
He took his two wives with him.
One wife was Ahinoam from Jezreel.
The other wife was Abigail.
Abigail had been the wife of Nabal from Carmel.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַל שָׁם֙ דָּוִ֔ד וְגַ֖ם שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשָׁ֑יו אֲחִינֹ֙עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֥ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽי׃

passages.text: David also took the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns near Hebron.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader chosen by God.
David had men who followed him.
Each man had his own household.
David took these men and their households with him.
They all went up together.
They settled in the towns near Hebron.
passages.original: וַאֲנָשָׁ֧יו אֲשֶׁר־ עִמּ֛וֹ הֶעֱלָ֥ה דָוִ֖ד אִ֣ישׁ וּבֵית֑וֹ וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בְּעָרֵ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then the men of Judah came to Hebron, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”
passages.sermon:
The men of Judah came to Hebron.
They anointed David as king over the house of Judah.
They told David about the men of Jabesh-gilead.
The men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּמְשְׁחוּ־ שָׁ֧ם אֶת־ דָּוִ֛ד לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַנְשֵׁי֙ יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָבְר֖וּ אֶת־ שָׁאֽוּל׃ס

passages.text: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to tell them, “The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead.
David spoke to the men of Jabesh-gilead through his messengers.
David said, “The LORD bless you.
You showed kindness to Saul, your lord.
You buried Saul.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־ אַנְשֵׁ֖י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם בְּרֻכִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֜ם הַחֶ֣סֶד הַזֶּ֗ה עִם־ אֲדֹֽנֵיכֶם֙ עִם־ שָׁא֔וּל וַֽתִּקְבְּר֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now may the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness, and I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.
passages.sermon:
David was the newly anointed king over the house of Judah.
David spoke to the men of Jabesh-gilead.
David said, “May the LORD show you kindness and truth.
You buried Saul, your lord.
You showed him kindness.
Because you did this, I will also do good to you.
I will show you the same favor.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֕ה יַֽעַשׂ־ יְהוָ֥ה עִמָּכֶ֖ם חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֑ת וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י אֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה אִתְּכֶם֙ הַטּוֹבָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Now then, be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to the men of Jabesh-gilead.
He told them about Saul’s death.
Saul was their lord.
David said, “Now be strong.
Be courageous.
Your lord Saul is dead.
The house of Judah has anointed me.
They made me king over them.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ תֶּחֱזַ֣קְנָה יְדֵיכֶ֗ם וִֽהְיוּ֙ לִבְנֵי־ חַ֔יִל כִּי־ מֵ֖ת אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֣ם שָׁא֑וּל וְגַם־ אֹתִ֗י מָשְׁח֧וּ בֵית־ יְהוּדָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Meanwhile, Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul’s army, took Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim, and made him king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin—over all Israel.
passages.sermon:
Abner was the son of Ner.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner took Ish-bosheth.
Ish-bosheth was the son of Saul.
Abner moved Ish-bosheth to Mahanaim.
Abner made Ish-bosheth king.
Ish-bosheth became king over Gilead.
Ish-bosheth became king over Asher.
Ish-bosheth became king over Jezreel.
Ish-bosheth became king over Ephraim.
Ish-bosheth became king over Benjamin.
Ish-bosheth became king over all Israel.
passages.original: וְאַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־ נֵ֔ר שַׂר־ צָבָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְשָׁא֑וּל לָקַ֗ח אֶת־ אִ֥ישׁ בֹּ֙שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־ שָׁא֔וּל וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖הוּ מַחֲנָֽיִם׃ וַיַּמְלִכֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד וְאֶל־ הָאֲשׁוּרִ֖י וְאֶֽל־ יִזְרְעֶ֑אל וְעַל־ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וְעַל־ בִּנְיָמִ֔ן וְעַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כֻּלֹּֽה׃פ

passages.text: Saul’s son Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years. The house of Judah, however, followed David.
passages.sermon:
Ish-bosheth was Saul’s son.
Ish-bosheth became king over Israel.
Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he began to reign.
Ish-bosheth reigned for two years.
The house of Judah did not follow Ish-bosheth.
The house of Judah followed David.
passages.original: בֶּן־ אַרְבָּעִ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה אִֽישׁ־ בֹּ֣שֶׁת בֶּן־ שָׁא֗וּל בְּמָלְכוֹ֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּשְׁתַּ֥יִם שָׁנִ֖ים מָלָ֑ךְ אַ֚ךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה הָי֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

passages.text: And the length of time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
passages.sermon:
David was king in Hebron.
He ruled over the house of Judah.
He was king there for seven years.
He was king there for six months.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפַּ֣ר הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה דָוִ֥ד מֶ֛לֶךְ בְּחֶבְר֖וֹן עַל־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃ס

passages.text: One day Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul marched out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
passages.sermon:
Abner was the son of Ner.
Ish-bosheth was the son of Saul.
Abner led the servants of Ish-bosheth.
They marched out from Mahanaim.
They went to Gibeon.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵא֙ אַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־ נֵ֔ר וְעַבְדֵ֖י אִֽישׁ־ בֹּ֣שֶׁת בֶּן־ שָׁא֑וּל מִֽמַּחֲנַ֖יִם גִּבְעֽוֹנָה׃

passages.text: So Joab son of Zeruiah, along with the servants of David, marched out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And the two camps took up positions on opposite sides of the pool.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah.
Joab led the servants of David.
Joab and David’s servants marched out.
They met Abner and his men by the pool of Gibeon.
The two groups stopped at the pool.
One group sat on one side of the pool.
The other group sat on the other side of the pool.
passages.original: וְיוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן־ צְרוּיָ֜ה וְעַבְדֵ֤י דָוִד֙ יָֽצְא֔וּ וַֽיִּפְגְּשׁ֛וּם עַל־ בְּרֵכַ֥ת גִּבְע֖וֹן יַחְדָּ֑ו וַיֵּ֨שְׁב֜וּ אֵ֤לֶּה עַל־ הַבְּרֵכָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥לֶּה עַל־ הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה מִזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then Abner said to Joab, “Let us have the young men get up and compete before us.” “Let them get up,” Joab replied.
passages.sermon:
Abner was the commander of Ish-bosheth’s army.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Abner spoke to Joab.
Abner said, “Let the young men get up.”
Abner said, “Let them compete in front of us.”
Joab answered Abner.
Joab said, “Let them get up.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְנֵר֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב יָק֤וּמוּ נָא֙ הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וִֽישַׂחֲק֖וּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יוֹאָ֖ב יָקֻֽמוּ׃

passages.text: So they got up and were counted off—twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve for David.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah.
Joab led the servants of David.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner served Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul.
Abner and Joab met at the pool of Gibeon.
Abner spoke to Joab.
Abner suggested that young men should compete before them.
Joab agreed.
The young men stood up.
They counted twelve men from the tribe of Benjamin.
These twelve men fought for Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul.
They also counted twelve men from the servants of David.
Each group had twelve men.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֖מוּ וַיַּעַבְר֣וּ בְמִסְפָּ֑ר שְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר לְבִנְיָמִ֗ן וּלְאִ֥ישׁ בֹּ֙שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־ שָׁא֔וּל וּשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר מֵעַבְדֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

passages.text: Then each man grabbed his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent’s side, and they all fell together. So this place, which is in Gibeon, is called Helkath-hazzurim.
passages.sermon:
Each man took hold of his opponent’s head.
Each man thrust his sword into his opponent’s side.
All the men fell together.
People called that place Helkath-hazzurim.
This place is in Gibeon.
passages.original: וַֽיַּחֲזִ֜קוּ אִ֣ישׁ׀ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ רֵעֵ֗הוּ וְחַרְבּוֹ֙ בְּצַ֣ד רֵעֵ֔הוּ וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ יַחְדָּ֑ו וַיִּקְרָא֙ לַמָּק֣וֹם הַה֔וּא חֶלְקַ֥ת הַצֻּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The battle that day was intense, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the servants of David.
passages.sermon:
The battle happened on that day.
The battle was very hard.
Abner led the men of Israel.
David had servants who fought for him.
Abner and the men of Israel lost the battle.
The servants of David defeated them.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֧י הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה קָשָׁ֥ה עַד־ מְאֹ֖ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיִּנָּ֤גֶף אַבְנֵר֙ וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

passages.text: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was fleet of foot like a wild gazelle, and he chased Abner, not turning to the right or to the left in his pursuit.
passages.sermon:
Three sons of Zeruiah were present.
Their names were Joab, Abishai, and Asahel.
Asahel could run very fast.
He was as swift as a wild gazelle in the field.
Asahel chased Abner.
He did not turn to the right.
He did not turn to the left.
He kept following Abner directly.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְיוּ־ שָׁ֗ם שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ בְּנֵ֣י צְרוּיָ֔ה יוֹאָ֥ב וַאֲבִישַׁ֖י וַעֲשָׂהאֵ֑ל וַעֲשָׂהאֵל֙ קַ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֔יו כְּאַחַ֥ד הַצְּבָיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃ וַיִּרְדֹּ֥ף עֲשָׂהאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֑ר וְלֹֽא־ נָטָ֣ה לָלֶ֗כֶת עַל־ הַיָּמִין֙ וְעַֽל־ הַשְּׂמֹ֔אול מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י אַבְנֵֽר׃

passages.text: And Abner glanced back and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” “It is,” Asahel replied.
passages.sermon:
Abner was a commander of Israel’s army.
Asahel was one of Zeruiah’s sons.
Abner looked behind him.
Abner spoke.
Abner said, “Are you Asahel?”
Asahel answered.
Asahel said, “I am.”
passages.original: וַיִּ֤פֶן אַבְנֵר֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה עֲשָׂהאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: So Abner told him, “Turn to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men, and take his equipment for yourself.” But Asahel would not stop chasing him.
passages.sermon:
Abner spoke to Asahel.
Abner told Asahel to turn aside.
Abner said, “Turn to your right or to your left.”
Abner told Asahel to seize one of the young men.
Abner told Asahel to take the young man’s equipment for himself.
Asahel did not stop chasing Abner.
Asahel refused to turn away from following Abner.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ אַבְנֵ֗ר נְטֵ֤ה לְךָ֙ עַל־ יְמִֽינְךָ֙ א֣וֹ עַל־ שְׂמֹאלֶ֔ךָ וֶאֱחֹ֣ז לְךָ֗ אֶחָד֙ מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְקַח־ לְךָ֖ אֶת־ חֲלִצָת֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֣ה עֲשָׂהאֵ֔ל לָס֖וּר מֵאַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: Once again, Abner warned Asahel, “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I show my face to your brother Joab?”
passages.sermon:
Abner was a military commander.
Asahel was chasing Abner.
Abner spoke to Asahel again.
Abner said, “Stop following me.”
Abner asked, “Why should I strike you down?”
Abner also asked, “How could I face your brother Joab if I harmed you?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧סֶף ע֣וֹד אַבְנֵ֗ר לֵאמֹר֙ אֶל־ עֲשָׂהאֵ֔ל ס֥וּר לְךָ֖ מֵאַֽחֲרָ֑י לָ֤מָּה אַכֶּ֙כָּה֙ אַ֔רְצָה וְאֵיךְ֙ אֶשָּׂ֣א פָנַ֔י אֶל־ יוֹאָ֖ב אָחִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: But Asahel refused to turn away; so Abner thrust the butt of his spear into his stomach, and it came out his back, and he fell dead on the spot. And every man paused when he came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died.
passages.sermon:
Asahel was a determined pursuer.
He refused to turn away from Abner.
Abner was a skilled warrior.
Abner struck Asahel with the back end of his spear.
Abner aimed at Asahel’s stomach.
The spear passed through Asahel’s body and came out his back.
Asahel fell down at that place.
Asahel died there.
Every man who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stopped there.
passages.original: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן לָס֗וּר וַיַּכֵּ֣הוּ אַבְנֵר֩ בְּאַחֲרֵ֨י הַחֲנִ֜ית אֶל־ הַחֹ֗מֶשׁ וַתֵּצֵ֤א הַֽחֲנִית֙ מֵאַחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּפָּל־ שָׁ֖ם וַיָּ֣מָת תַּחַתוֹ וַיְהִ֡י כָּל־ הַבָּ֣א אֶֽל־ הַמָּקוֹם֩ אֲשֶׁר־ נָ֨פַל שָׁ֧ם עֲשָׂהאֵ֛ל וַיָּמֹ֖ת וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽדוּ׃

passages.text: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. By sunset, they had gone as far as the hill of Ammah opposite Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander of David’s army.
Abishai was Joab’s brother.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Joab and Abishai chased Abner.
The sun was setting.
Joab and Abishai reached the hill of Ammah.
This hill was across from Giah.
The hill was on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.
passages.original: וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֛וּ יוֹאָ֥ב וַאֲבִישַׁ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֑ר וְהַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ בָּ֔אָה וְהֵ֗מָּה בָּ֚אוּ עַד־ גִּבְעַ֣ת אַמָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־ פְּנֵי־ גִ֔יחַ דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר גִּבְעֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The Benjamites rallied to Abner, formed a single unit, and took their stand atop a hill.
passages.sermon:
The Benjamites followed Abner.
They gathered together.
They became one group.
They stood on top of a hill.
passages.original: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ בִנְיָמִן֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיִּהְי֖וּ לַאֲגֻדָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ עַ֥ל רֹאשׁ־ גִּבְעָ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃

passages.text: Then Abner called out to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness? How long before you tell the troops to stop pursuing their brothers?”
passages.sermon:
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Abner called out to Joab.
Abner said, “Must the sword keep killing forever?”
Abner said, “You know this will end in bitterness.”
Abner said, “How long until you tell the people to stop chasing their brothers?”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְנֵ֜ר אֶל־ יוֹאָ֗ב וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הֲלָנֶ֙צַח֙ תֹּ֣אכַל חֶ֔רֶב הֲל֣וֹא יָדַ֔עְתָּה כִּֽי־ מָרָ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה בָּאַחֲרוֹנָ֑ה וְעַד־ מָתַי֙ לֹֽא־ תֹאמַ֣ר לָעָ֔ם לָשׁ֖וּב מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: “As surely as God lives,” Joab replied, “if you had not spoken up, the troops would have continued pursuing their brothers until morning.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab spoke to Abner.
Joab said, “As surely as God lives.”
Joab said, “If you had not spoken.”
Joab said, “The troops would have kept pursuing their brothers.”
Joab said, “They would have done this until morning.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֔ב חַ֚י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֥י לוּלֵ֖א דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ כִּ֣י אָ֤ז מֵֽהַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ נַעֲלָ֣ה הָעָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: So Joab blew the ram’s horn, and all the troops stopped; they no longer pursued Israel or continued to fight.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab blew the ram’s horn.
All the troops stopped.
They did not pursue Israel anymore.
They did not continue to fight.
passages.original: וַיִּתְקַ֤ע יוֹאָב֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ כָּל־ הָעָ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ יִרְדְּפ֥וּ ע֖וֹד אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹֽא־ יָסְפ֥וּ ע֖וֹד לְהִלָּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: And all that night Abner and his men marched through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, marched all morning, and arrived at Mahanaim.
passages.sermon:
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner led his men.
They marched through the Arabah all night.
They crossed the Jordan River.
They continued marching through the morning.
They arrived at Mahanaim.
passages.original: וְאַבְנֵ֣ר וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֗יו הָֽלְכוּ֙ בָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה כֹּ֖ל הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיַּעַבְר֣וּ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ כָּל־ הַבִּתְר֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מַחֲנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: When Joab returned from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops. In addition to Asahel, nineteen of David’s servants were missing, but they had struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab returned after he had chased Abner.
Joab gathered all the troops together.
They counted the men who served David.
Nineteen of David’s servants were missing.
Asahel was also missing.
David’s men had fought against the men of Benjamin.
David’s men had also fought against Abner’s men.
David’s men killed three hundred sixty men from Benjamin and from Abner’s group.
passages.original: וְיוֹאָ֗ב שָׁ֚ב מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיִּקְבֹּ֖ץ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֑ם וַיִּפָּ֨קְד֜וּ מֵעַבְדֵ֥י דָוִ֛ד תִּשְׁעָֽה־ עָשָׂ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ וַעֲשָׂה־ אֵֽל׃ וְעַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד הִכּוּ֙ מִבִּנְיָמִ֔ן וּבְאַנְשֵׁ֖י אַבְנֵ֑ר שְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֧וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֛ים אִ֖ישׁ מֵֽתוּ׃

passages.text: Later, they took Asahel and buried him in his father’s tomb in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander of David’s army.
Asahel was Joab’s brother.
Joab and his men took Asahel’s body.
They buried Asahel in his father’s tomb.
This tomb was in Bethlehem.
After the burial, Joab and his men traveled all night.
They arrived in Hebron at daybreak.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־ עֲשָׂהאֵ֔ל וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֙הוּ֙ בְּקֶ֣בֶר אָבִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ כָל־ הַלַּ֗יְלָה יוֹאָב֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו וַיֵּאֹ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃
